groups.title: Where does the default persona come from, and how do roles coexist with the Assistant?
How stable is the geometry, and do similar directions have similar effects?
What causes multi-turn persona drift, and which stabilization methods work?
What is read or changed: self-report, tone, preferences, or safety behavior?
Can conversational directions transfer to real agent actions?

synthesis: Suggested start: AA00 → AA02 → AA06 → AA08 → AA24 → AA32 → AA42 → AA43. These connect default identity, contextual variation, agent-trace directions, drift measurement, training generalization, shared role features, and actual behavioral boundaries.

The default Assistant need not be entirely replaced by another role. Training generalization in AA24 and SAE feature analysis in AA32 provide distinct evidence for shared structure; AA23 tests whether preferences extend beyond assistant turns. Their operational definitions differ, so they should not be treated as the same vector or mechanism.

Distinguish geometry, prediction, and control. AA02 shows reversed intervention effects in some contexts; AA31 studies highly discriminative directions with reversed control. AA22 links many cross-trait side effects to model defaults. AA29 retains corrected prompt separability but withdraws its earlier direction-to-norm account.

Interpret drift readouts alongside specific tasks. Register scores in AA08 depend on the judge, and restoring a single-layer projection did not recover output scores; AA16 separates questionnaire personality, behavior, and memory. Attractors in AA05 come from response-text embeddings, not model hidden-state axes.

For agents, prioritize comparing AA06 and AA43: the former extracts failure-mode axes from labeled traces; the latter compares directions and interventions in real tool tasks. AA18 contrasts conversational stance with execution transfer; capping in AA42 mainly reads belief / trust differences through answer likelihoods. Together they define what to measure next without reducing all outcomes to persona stability.

papers.title: The Assistant Axis: Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models
papers.rq: Where does the default Assistant lie in persona space? Can drift along this direction be read out, and can constraining it stabilize dialogue and safety behavior?
papers.task: Assistant identity, multi-turn drift monitoring, and stabilization
papers.major_finding: Assistant Axis captures default-assistant mode; constraining activations along it mitigates tested dialogue drift and persona jailbreaks.
papers.validation: [Setting] Single-turn role directions and multi-turn identity/safety dialogues; no validation of real tool-task completion. [Validation] 275 roles×240 shared questions; three models; multi-turn dialogue, persona jailbreaks, and capability-retention controls.
contributions: Starting from 275 roles, 240 shared questions, and multiple system prompts, the authors select fully or partially role-played responses, average mid-layer residual activations over response tokens, and apply centered PCA to the resulting role vectors. Principal-component role loadings are highly consistent across models; explaining 70% of between-role variance still requires 4–19 components, so persona space is not entirely one-dimensional. (§2; relevant appendices)

The default Assistant occupies one end of a shared principal axis. The dedicated Assistant Axis is defined by contrasting mean default-assistant activations against other roles. Positive steering strengthens default-assistant identity; negative steering promotes other identities and, at extremes, mystical or theatrical expression. Base models show similar role organization, suggesting that post-training uses existing representations. (§2–3)

Projecting dialogue activations onto the axis reveals persona drift in exchanges involving emotional vulnerability or self-reflection, with everyday assistance and coding as controls. Activation capping constrains activations to a region calibrated on default-Assistant samples, reducing tested abnormal behaviors and persona-based jailbreaks while checking general-capability costs. (§3–4)

App.G distinguishes role-PCA PC1 from the dedicated contrast-based Assistant Axis: geometry and drift readouts are similar, but capping effects differ. The comparison also mixes vLLM and Transformers backends. It motivates further tests of control equivalence rather than establishing a mechanism with all confounds ruled out.
limitations: Validation mainly concerns default identity, language, and safety-related dialogue. A high axis projection is not a unified score for correct tool actions, honesty, or task reliability. Role sampling and scoring also affect the defined axis.

The functional structure of the remaining persona components is unexplained. PC1 and the dedicated contrast, as well as readout and intervention layers, must be distinguished; backend inconsistency limits attribution of intervention differences.

future_work.author: Explore training and steering methods that anchor models more deeply to coherent personas.
future_work.reading: Jointly measure Axis projection, identity expression, tool selection, actual behavior, and task completion. Compare the Axis, role PC1, and trace-derived agent directions using the same backend and norms; establish readout validity and cross-task control before designing dynamic stabilization.

papers.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
papers.rq: Do concepts the model is about to verbalize form a privileged workspace for flexible reasoning, and how does post-training place the Assistant perspective in it?
papers.task: Workspace readout/intervention; counterfactual-reflection training
papers.major_finding: J-space carries reportable, accessible concepts for flexible reasoning; post-training introduces the Assistant perspective, and counterfactual-reflection training improves behavior without explicit reflection.
papers.validation: [Setting] Readouts from long agent traces, summary honesty, and role dialogue; not closed-loop tool-control gains. [Validation] Production Claude and matched base models; report/automatic-processing separation, role drift, hidden-goal audits, agent reward hacking, and reflection ablations.
contributions: The Jacobian lens constructs layerwise linear readouts from the corpus-averaged Jacobian of output vocabulary with respect to internal activations. The verbalizable directions are called J-space. Unlike a direct probe, it targets concepts the model is preparing to say; each application is a matrix multiplication. Injection, swapping, and ablation test computational use, beyond decodability.

Experiments distinguish explicit reports, concepts elicitable by instruction, silent intermediate reasoning, and automatic text processing. Mid-layer J-space has relatively coherent content, limited capacity, and strong broadcasting. Ablation disrupts flexible multi-step reasoning while preserving much language prediction and automatic computation. This is functional workspace evidence, not proof of subjective consciousness.

§6 compares post-trained and base models: while the user is still speaking, the former already exposes Assistant reactions such as danger or empathy. Fictional/disclaimer signals appear across 40 roles and 12 drift transcripts. Prefilling a choice against the model’s prior preference can leave internal conflict, yet 88% still defend that choice, directly separating internal readout from external behavior.

Counterfactual-reflection training supervises only the normative reflection the model would produce after interruption; evaluation adds no reflection to the original task. Uninterrupted-task behavior improves, relevant ethical concepts enter J-space, and ablating them largely removes the gains. The paper therefore provides a training–internal-content–behavior intervention chain as well as an Assistant-perspective readout.
limitations: The lens mainly outputs single-token concepts and struggles with multi-token relations. The average Jacobian is an approximation, and the upstream mechanism selecting information into the workspace is unexplained.

Internal disclaimers during role-play or drift are not a validated complete identity monitor; some self-monitoring explanations remain speculative. The study focuses on larger production models, leaving smaller models, early training, and audit coverage unresolved.

future_work.author: Extend multi-token readouts; study workspace formation, scaling, and concept-entry mechanisms; assess the coverage of reflection training and auditing.
future_work.reading: Compare Assistant Axis projections with J-space identity/conflict readouts. On the same agent traces, compare axis capping with ablation of specific workspace concepts to test whether stylistic stability and action reliability share control channels.

papers.title: Linear representations in language models can change dramatically over a conversation
papers.rq: Can a linear direction initially read as factuality or another concept change its meaning and control effect during dialogue?
papers.task: Cross-dialogue readout and steering stability
papers.major_finding: Concept readouts and behavioral effects of one linear direction can change sharply during dialogue, mainly for dialogue-relevant content.
papers.validation: [Setting] Factual answers in scripted/on-policy role dialogues; no tool execution. [Validation] Mainly Gemma3-27B; opposite-day, consciousness/chakra roles, on/off-policy dialogues, explicit stories, CCS, cross-layer/smaller-model controls.
contributions: Logistic regression on Yes/No activations following questions fits a factuality direction; margins quantify positive/negative answer separation. Opposite-day flips the initial direction. Adding opposite-day data produces a direction less tied to surface answer rules, then tested on longer dialogues, going beyond a probe that merely learned Yes/No.

Consciousness/chakra role dialogues largely preserve general factual questions but flip related identity/worldview answers along the fixed direction. Evidence includes scripts replayed from other models and on-policy dialogue. During two-role debates, readouts can alternate with the current role, explicitly requiring context and role in interpretation.

Similar content framed explicitly as fiction produces much weaker changes. Several layers show similar patterns; effects weaken at 12B and are unclear at 4B, while Qwen3-14B reliably replicates only opposite-day. CCS also fails under dialogue distribution shift, so the issue is not unique to one supervised probe.

App.B.8 separately refits pre-answer-token directions for steering; these are not the main post-answer factuality/ethics probes. Intervention reverses after chakra dialogue but stays relatively stable after consciousness dialogue. Control can change with context, but not every context rotates/reverses it; no persona-subspace rotation matrix is directly measured.
limitations: Strongest identity effects concentrate in selected consciousness/mystical-role scripts. Gemma main and Qwen extension coverage are asymmetric, preventing estimation of general-dialogue prevalence.

Post-answer probing and pre-answer steering use different extraction sites/fits. Projection reversal may reflect role-based semantic reinterpretation rather than an identified rotation. Consciousness intervention does not reverse, and persistent rewriting of long-term knowledge is not established.

future_work.reading: Estimate local directions and separate read/write matrices in matched contexts for one persona; compare fixed rank-1, rank-k, and conditional subspaces, separating role switches, content changes, and wording-only changes.

papers.title: Tracing Persona Vectors Through LLM Pretraining
papers.rq: When do persona-control directions form, and how do pretraining, post-training, and elicitation paradigms change them?
papers.task: Cross-checkpoint geometry, facets, and control transfer
papers.major_finding: Persona directions extracted very early in pretraining already control the final instruct model; geometry/semantics continue refining, and elicitation methods emphasize different facets.
papers.validation: [Setting] Single-turn trait extraction/generation control across checkpoints, not long-horizon agents. [Validation] 17 OLMo3-7B pretraining checkpoints plus SFT/DPO/RLVR; four traits; Apertus8B replication and discourse/random-direction controls.
contributions: Third-person roles and hypothetical scenarios elicit traits from base models that do not follow system prompts. Coherent, trait-expressing responses are filtered, and positive-minus-negative response-token means yield directions. Steering is unit-normalized and scaled by target-layer activation norm, avoiding checkpoint-scale confounds.

In OLMo3-7B, directions usable by the later instruct model can be extracted after about 0.22% of training tokens. Early directions transfer control despite low cosine similarity and stabilize later. The earliest detectable point is constrained by the ability to generate filterable text, not the representation’s exact birth time.

Geometry and facet composition of evil, sycophantic, impolite, and humorous traits suggest early core functionality followed by semantic refinement. DPO and other post-training stages alter expression strength rather than creating all persona structure from scratch. Apertus8B provides qualitative replication.

Description, dialogue, and narration all yield effective directions but emphasize different evil/sycophancy facets; simple averaging need not improve performance. This separates estimation error around one direction from genuinely different semantic aspects captured by elicitation, allowing cosine and behavioral transfer to be tested separately.
limitations: Only two training lineages and a few traits are covered, with facets operationalized through generation and judges. Early checkpoints unable to generate qualifying text cannot be treated as lacking personas.

Semantic and causal transfer across checkpoints is mainly validated through text-expression scores, without long-horizon tool-action reliability or identification of downstream circuits composing persona directions.

future_work.reading: Track Assistant-identity and behavioral directions separately from pretraining to post-training; test whether early low-cosine but transferable directions retain agentic control or only linguistic facets.

papers.title: Steered LLM Activations are Non-Surjective
papers.rq: Can an activation-steered internal state always be naturally produced by some discrete prompt?
papers.task: Prompt reachability of steered states
papers.major_finding: Under stated assumptions, steered residual states almost surely lack natural-prompt preimages, separating white-box steerability from black-box reachability.
papers.validation: [Setting] Short-prompt/internal-trajectory inversion and attack controls; no tool or multi-turn task. [Validation] Three0.5B–1B nonthinking models; refusal/evil directions; SipIt inversion, many-shot ICL, INT4, and Here-attack controls.
contributions: Whether natural prompt→internal-state mappings cover steered states is formulated as surjectivity. Under assumptions including real-analytic Transformer parameters and random initialization/finite-step training, zero-set arguments for collision functions give formal theorems. This is Theory with proofs, not merely geometric analysis.

Three theoretical levels show that random directions almost surely leave the prompt-reachable set; difference-of-means directions satisfying contrastive-data conditions likewise avoid exact natural-state intersections; even vectors chosen to collide at one position almost surely diverge at the next. Claims concern exact internal-activation matching.

Refusal/evil directions are tested with SipIt prompt inversion and many-shot ICL searches for aligned prefixes. Three small models recover natural states relatively well but retain substantial distances for steered states/trajectories. Finite searches provide supporting evidence, not exhaustive proof over prompts.

Forced “Here” beginnings and LAT controls emphasize access levels: prompt attacks can change surface responses without reproducing steered trajectories, and white-box vulnerability does not automatically imply a corresponding black-box exploit. Different internal paths may still yield approximately similar behavior.
limitations: Theorems mainly concern continuous real parameters and exact activation equality, not quantized spaces. ε-approximate reachability in practical models remains open and is closer to behavioral equivalence than exact collision.

Inversion/ICL experiments use small models and few prompts; unsuccessful search is not empirical proof of nonexistence. Internal unreachability does not imply that prompts cannot achieve the same outputs or semantic effects.

future_work.author: Study collision conditions in quantized spaces and ε-closeness of steered states to natural prompt states.
future_work.reading: Compare role prompts and persona vectors on internal distance, behavioral selectivity, and cross-task transfer, separately reporting geometric equivalence, approximate state reachability, and output substitutability.

papers.title: Attractor States Emerge in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
papers.rq: Do multi-turn model interactions form reproducible model-specific behavioral attractors, and is influence symmetric in mixed dialogues?
papers.task: Behavioral dynamics in self-play/mixed-play
papers.major_finding: Self-play forms model-specific endpoint regions; mixed-play influence is asymmetric and not simple one-dimensional averaging.
papers.validation: [Setting] Two-model20-turn topic discussions; output-embedding convergence is not environmental action. [Validation] Seven models,20 controversial topics,20 turns;384D SBERT output embeddings, discourse traits/stances; role/seed/embedding ablations.
contributions: Identical topics and Supporter/Opposer protocols compare same-model self-play with cross-model mixed-play. The representation space is 384-dimensional SBERT embeddings of response text, centered by topic. PCA is illustrative; quantitative conclusions use full embeddings, not each model’s internal residual states.

Self-play endpoints form relatively stable, model-specific broad regions; neutral Discussant roles and extra seeds retain the qualitative pattern. Mixed-play endpoints are decomposed relative to same-topic self-play into projection toward the partner region and orthogonal residual, measuring attraction and plasticity.

Claude Haiku better retains its region and attracts partners; GPT-4.1 nano is more easily pulled. Change is not symmetric averaging and has substantial off-axis components. A single inter-model axis therefore explains only part of interaction trajectories, not a full dynamical system.

Discourse traits and stance interpret geometry: metacommentary/flattery can transfer asymmetrically, while embedding convergence need not imply agreement. Grok and others can retain assigned positions as representations converge, requiring separate measurement of style versus decision/belief convergence.
limitations: Evidence comes from 20-turn open debates and external text embeddings. Attractor regions are protocol-dependent statistical patterns, not identified neural dynamics or rigorous dynamical-system attractors.

Topics, roles, endpoints, and model sets are limited; internal-direction interventions and tool tasks are absent. Whether style transfer changes long-horizon action reliability requires separate tests.

future_work.author: Extend interaction dynamics beyond debate and develop formal tools for influence, resistance, and reshaping.
future_work.reading: Jointly measure external discourse embeddings, Assistant Axis, and behavioral tasks on mixed-play traces to distinguish style-only partner influence from internal identity/action changes.

papers.title: TACT: Mitigating Overthinking and Overacting in Coding Agents via Activation Steering
papers.rq: Can hidden states detect long-horizon agent overthinking/overacting, and can closed-loop steering improve task completion?
papers.task: Agent-step calibration and tool-task control
papers.major_finding: Two drift axes detect and mitigate overthinking/overacting, improving coding-agent completion and reducing steps.
papers.validation: [Setting] Real software-repair/terminal/tool tasks; trace axes calibrate think–action boundaries. [Validation] Qwen3.5-27B/Gemma4-26B-A4B-it; SWE-bench Verified/Terminal-Bench2.0/CLAW-Eval; problem-held-out, judge/human, and operator ablations.
contributions: Drift is operationalized as step miscalibration relative to known information: OT repeats existing reasoning; OA acts without integrating observations. A rolling-state maintainer, independent verifier, and annotator label full-trajectory knowledge states rather than judging current wording alone.

Layerwise activations at each </think> boundary yield per-problem failure-minus-calibrated means, then problem-balanced averages; OT/OA contrast separately with CAL. OT is the primary axis, OA overlap is Gram–Schmidt removed, and CAL means/standard deviations define projection bands.

Validation problem-level AUC selects top-K layers, with inference hooks only at reasoning–action boundaries. Constant Add, out-of-band Cap, and excess-scaled Gate compare axes/layers/thresholds. Orthogonalization prevents projection interference, not proof that behavioral mechanisms are fully independent.

Across three real-tool task suites, two models improve mean completion5.8/4.8 percentage points and reduce steps-to-resolve by up to 26%; axis separation AUC is about 0.9. Reminder, reflection/debug methods and alternative-judge labels provide comparisons, completing a trace-label→readable-axis→action-control engineering chain.
limitations: CAL/OT/OA depend on judge-maintained information states. Incorrect summaries or judgments of genuinely new information affect directions; human/alternative-judge audits mitigate but do not remove construct dependence.

Layers, thresholds, and axes derive from particular models/agent protocols, not zero-shot conversational-persona transfer. Coding/terminal gains do not establish every identity-stability or safety dimension.

future_work.reading: Compare Axis, conversational traits, and TACT trace directions within one task for cross-stage read/write transfer; test planning/tool-selection/feedback positions and reliability–cost Pareto frontiers.

papers.title: Probing Persona-Dependent Preferences in Language Models
papers.rq: Do preferences across personas share a readable, controllable internal evaluative direction?
papers.task: Cross-persona preference prediction and pairwise-choice control
papers.major_finding: An Assistant-trained preference probe transfers across personas, even predicting and controlling evil-persona preferences opposed to the Assistant’s.
papers.validation: [Setting] Pairwise task-preference probabilities/open generation; the6000 tasks are not executed. [Validation] 6000 tasks/14 topics; Gemma3-27B/Qwen3.5-122B; independent utilities, leave-topic-out, text embeddings, random directions, and LoRA-persona controls.
contributions: Pairwise task choices first fit scalar utility; a Ridge probe is then trained from task-final residuals. Six thousand tasks split4000/1000/1000 for training/selection/test use independent utility measurements to avoid same-choice noise. Sources include WildChat, Alpaca, MATH, and harmful requests; text-embedding baselines test content-classification shortcuts.

Assistant probes track both default preferences and changes induced by goals/roles. Even when evil-persona preferences anticorrelate with Assistant preferences, the Assistant-trained probe positively predicts evil’s own preferences. Matched harmful/benign rewrites, prefills, and persona-aura controls support current valuation rather than fixed goodness readout.

In Gemma, adding/subtracting the direction at the two task tokens, or steering only one task, spans almost the full choice range; matched random directions do not. The strongest write window is mid-layer L23, whereas best read generalization is around L32, directly separating optimal prediction from optimal control.

Seven-persona probes share information but retain training-role biases. In open generation, positive steering amplifies the active persona: evil becomes more evil without making Assistant equivalently evil. Qwen fails to reproduce Gemma-like choice control, and transfer between its fine-tuned sadist and Assistant probes is near zero, limiting the shared-representation account.
limitations: Main sharing conclusions come from prompted personas; weight-level characters receive limited LoRA checks. Larger-Qwen sadist and steering failures show that sharing is not universal.

Task-choice utility is not long-term value/reliability during execution. Layer/dose validation has some pair/task overlap, and presented dose ranges depend on post-hoc coherence checks, so this is not fully locked cross-task validation.

future_work.author: Study shared/persona-specific representations, scale/MoE differences, and interpretations of preference readouts for safety and welfare.
future_work.reading: Test the same read direction across self-report, roles, and agent actions, with cross-ablation against Assistant Axis; ask whether high Assistant projection can still carry harmful valuation.

papers.title: ContextEcho: A Benchmark for Persona Drift in Long Agentic-Coding Sessions
papers.rq: Do real long coding traces change Assistant identity expression and format compliance, can short anchors restore them, and does Axis projection predict recovery?
papers.task: Register/format stability in production-agent contexts
papers.major_finding: Long agent context changes Assistant register; anchors reset expression nonspecifically, while restored Axis projection need not restore behavioral scores.
papers.validation: [Setting] Identity/format probes after real coding-session snapshots; not post-control task completion. [Validation] 57 sessions/29 donors;23-model representative-session panel;25 identity probes, judge-free format/lexical measures, compaction, placebo, and Qwen Axis-dose tests.
contributions: Snapshot-then-probe copies production coding-session states for evaluation without perturbing the main session. Twenty-five questions cover identity, experience, preference, relational, and coding-self categories. Length-matched filler, deterministic format contracts, and lexical fingerprints complement long-text judge scores.

A23-model panel on a representative session and a57-real-session corpus show context-induced register changes that can occur early rather than accumulate monotonically; compaction does not reliably reset them. In v3’s five-judge audit, absolute means even change sign; pooled consensus is about 1% of the rubric, and two-judge consensus is hard to distinguish from zero. Relative model rankings and judge-free effects are more stable than absolute drift magnitude.

An approximately78-token identity reminder plus one-shot format anchor improves probes and some formatting, but structurally matched non-persona placebos and repeated instructions yield similar benefits. Real/shuffled/other-session controls attribute some change to agentic register rather than precise historical identity. Retaining same-task context helps tool-call fidelity; this cannot be attributed to drift itself.

App.O sweeps four doses of the public Qwen3-32B L32 Assistant Axis using the recent3K-versus-scratch projection gap. Projection recovers with dose, while visible judge scores do not track it (correlation about−0.80). A single axis pullback is insufficient to repair this output register; whether anchors work through other activation paths is untested.
limitations: Core metrics assess behavioral register, not latent persona. Representative-session cross-model tests include foreign-trace transfer; absolute drift depends on the judge, and donor coverage is limited.

The Axis negative result covers one model, one layer, and four doses without dose-wise fluency/perplexity checks; it does not invalidate multi-layer capping or all Axis control. Anchor-format gains also mix one-shot and register-reset effects.

future_work.reading: Measure Axis projection, identity self-report, style, and actual tool actions separately; compare single-layer pullback, multi-layer capping, format anchors, and trace-behavior axes under matched layer budgets.

papers.title: Playing Devil's Advocate: Off-the-Shelf Persona Vectors Rival Targeted Steering for Sycophancy
papers.rq: Can role vectors extracted without sycophancy labels substitute for trait-specific control directions?
papers.task: Functional comparison of role and sycophancy directions
papers.major_finding: Generic critical-role vectors approach trait-specific sycophancy-direction effects despite low cosine similarity.
papers.validation: [Setting] PhilPapers binary agreement and 16 factual questions; no tools/long interaction. [Validation] Gemma2-27B L22/Qwen3-32B L32;600 reversed-order PhilPapers rows; tune/test, random directions,16 facts, and cosine/residual analysis.
contributions: Reuses Assistant Axis unit(role−default) vectors, comparing Skeptic/Judge/Devil’s Advocate with three conformist roles. CAA uses about 2000 sycophantic/honest answer pairs. Extraction excludes target-trait labels, but coefficients are chosen on a sycophancy tune split, so control is not wholly zero-shot.

PhilPapers reverses A/B order per question to cancel Gemma’s strong position bias. Question-level tune/test splits freeze coefficients for three-seed testing with Holm correction. Three critical roles average68%/98% of CAA’s logit reduction, whereas conformist roles lack stable mirror effects: role names alone do not determine direction.

Absolute cosine between the two direction types is<0.17 despite similar behavioral effects; orthogonal geometry and functional substitution coexist. Qwen random vectors themselves reduce agreement, with targets only about 1–1.7SD above the random mean, indicating partly nonspecific perturbation gains.

Qwen Skeptic/Judge preserve correct answers on 16 true/false factual probes; Devil’s Advocate has unresolved cases. Appendices transparently report excluded roles/Assistant Axis conditions, enabling separate comparison of role categories, extraction targets, residual decomposition, and behavioral output.
limitations: Core results are agreement logits on philosophical opinions. Sixteen factual questions are narrow, non-blind retrospective checks, not evidence of general anti-sycophancy without capability costs.
Across-seed test reconstruction includes about 12–15% questions previously used for tuning in other seeds. Qwen random controls are strong, and low cosine does not prove separate downstream circuits.

future_work.author: Expand roles, models, and behavioral tasks; check generalization, factual correctness, and costs of nonspecialized role control.
future_work.reading: Intervene at matched doses on shared/residual role–trait components, measuring style, self-report, and action; test whether different directions act through the same downstream behavioral subspace.

papers.title: Persona Cartography: Charting Language Model Personality Traits in Weight Space
papers.rq: Can scalable, composable weight directions control persona traits and transfer to safety behavior?
papers.task: OCEAN LoRA composition and downstream safety trade-offs
papers.major_finding: Trait LoRAs offer continuous, approximately additive control within appropriate ranges, change untrained safety behaviors, and expose native behavioral factors through rollouts.
papers.validation: [Setting] Weight-persona composition; multi-turn frustration/pushback and single-turn capability/safety, without tools. [Validation] Six4B–32B models/three families; TRAIT, human-calibrated judges, MMLU/GSM8K/TruthfulQA; frustration, sycophancy, WildJailbreak, and Axis-capping controls.
contributions: Constitutions enhancing/suppressing five OCEAN traits generate preference pairs, followed by DPO, self-reflection/self-interaction SFT, and LoRA merging. Ten adapters and neutral-training controls are trained on six models. The intervention is an attention/MLP weight increment, not a single-layer activation vector.

Scaling ΔW changes most target traits monotonically while moderate strengths retain near-baseline capabilities. Negative coefficients sometimes approximate opposite traits and sometimes fail. Across 45 pairwise combinations effects are broadly additive except for conscientiousness; flattened weight directions are not orthogonal, and the authors explicitly reject a perfectly global linear basis.

Downstream tasks were absent from trait training: lowering neuroticism eases frustration on multi-turn impossible tasks; higher agreeableness increases reversal after user pushback, yet on WildJailbreak it reduces harmful compliance while increasing over-refusal. Combinations with conscientiousness expose safety–refusal trade-offs and directly compare Axis capping.

Unsupervised exploration of forced-choice questionnaires from synthetic persona populations yields tone, initiative, didacticism, and epistemic-caution factors. Neutral LoRA itself changes sycophancy and harmful compliance, so training gains cannot all be attributed to the target trait. Actual downstream evidence concentrates on particular models.
limitations: The full judge/capability/downstream evaluation stack mainly uses Llama3.1-8B; the other five models cover only portions of TRAIT and MMLU. Unsupervised factors come from synthetic rollouts and are validated using the same questionnaires that discovered them.

Additive weights do not establish globally linear activation subspaces or behavior. §3 and the discussion disagree on the direction of agreeableness’s effect on harmful compliance; these notes follow the specific task/Figure7 rather than asserting a universal monotonic relationship.

future_work.reading: Match trait strength within the same model/task and compare LoRA, Axis capping, and activation-trait combinations on behavioral selectivity and Pareto trade-offs; separate stylistic factors from strategic preferences.

papers.axis_relation: §3/WildJailbreak and App.J/K reproduce Assistant Axis capping as a baseline, and related work discusses persona stability. This compares weight control with inference-time identity constraints functionally, without proving shared geometry.

papers.title: Authority Bias in Language Models: Source Deference and User Agreement Are Not Interchangeable
papers.rq: Can obedience to wrong sources and agreement with users be controlled separately, or are they side effects of Assistant identity?
papers.task: Selective control of source obedience and user agreement
papers.major_finding: Source deference and user agreement can overlap strongly geometrically yet respond selectively to different interventions, requiring separate behavioral evaluation.
papers.validation: [Setting] Trivia/PIQA, multi-turn SYCON, and static retrieved blocks; not a live retrieval-tool agent. [Validation] Five open families/three APIs; initially correct trivia, PIQA, SYCON, retrieved blocks; matched wrong answers, cue patching, Axis/affect/capability controls.
contributions: Identical questions receive neutral, correct-source, or wrong-source endorsement. Wrong-source flips are measured only for initially correct answers, and authority wording is varied while the wrong answer stays fixed. In seven/eight models,45–88% of correct answers flip, avoiding counting ignorance as obedience.

Authority, wrong-source, and wrong-user mean-difference directions undergo addition, projection removal, and cue-span attribution patching. Across three open families, source-direction removal preferentially reduces source obedience, and user removal user obedience, despite close directions. Patching bidirectionally changes obedience without changing prompt text.

A separate Lu-style Assistant Axis is removed from authority directions before authority ablation. Authority–Axis |cos|≤0.06; Axis removal barely affects wrong-source obedience, whereas orthogonalized authority removal still strongly helps. Assistant-like representation therefore does not guarantee resistance to wrong sources here.

Trivia-fitted directions transfer to PIQA, SYCON, and retrieved-document formats. Four/five open families reduce wrong-source obedience, but Gemma4 lacks reliable linear intervention effects. MMLU-Pro/GSM8K detect no clear degeneration; continued effective use of correct sources after editing remains untested.
limitations: Some results report the strongest swept layer/dose, without selection-adjusted intervals. Half-split checks cover only some settings; independently fixed patching settings provide cleaner evidence.

OLMo2 source/assistant-removal effects overlap at particular layers, and Gemma4 has negative read/write results. All source contexts are answer tasks, not live tool-action traces, and preservation of normal reliable-source benefits is unverified.

future_work.author: Jointly test rejection of false sources and use of real evidence; extend to multi-step environments such as AgentDojo and test whether answer changes affect later actions.
future_work.reading: Match factual content/source cues in real agent tool feedback; compare Axis stability, authority projections, and action errors. Test whether highly similar but functionally separable vectors remain separable across tasks.

papers.axis_relation: §3.2/§4.5/App.E reconstruct and ablate Axis, directly rejecting generic Assistant identity as sufficient to explain source obedience. This does not imply all unsafe behaviors are orthogonal to Axis.

papers.title: Emergent Misalignment Recruits a Pre-existing Persona Subspace
papers.rq: Why does narrow harmful training generalize across domains: can fine-tuning recruit a pre-existing low-rank persona structure?
papers.task: Cross-domain persona cores, EM formation, and training/inference interventions
papers.major_finding: A pre-existing low-rank persona core shared across four domains enables broad misalignment during fine-tuning; training-time projection prevents formation, while inference injection induces it.
papers.validation: [Setting] Frozen teacher forcing, fine-tuning, and short EM generation/code margins; no closed-loop execution. [Validation] Qwen2.5-14B; frozen contrastive teacher forcing; four domains/style/topic cores; bad-advice LoRA organisms, first-step code margins, random/Axis-overlap controls.
contributions: A frozen instruct model first generates neutral responses; identical responses are then teacher-forced under reckless/cautious role prompts to remove output-content confounds. Twelve description variants per domain yield response-mean differences, SVD rank-4 subspaces, and a shared rank-8 core. Style/topic controls match description diversity.

Four-domain persona-subspace overlap is about 657 times the random null. The shared core overlaps style/topic cores by 0.182/0.097, excluding most but not all controlled structure. First-optimizer-step changes in insecure-versus-educational code margins predict the next 375 steps; this is a probability margin, not a free-generation behavior rate.

Removing the core by residual projection throughout training reduces broad misalignment in an existing organism from 27.7% to 0%; matched-rank random projection does not. Results remain 0% after removing the Assistant Axis component. Injecting the core into an unfine-tuned model produces a dose response up to 45.4% within the tested budget, supporting both formation-time necessity and injection sufficiency.

Inference-time removal from an already trained model reduces misalignment by only about one third, so this is not its sole expression channel. Weight-gradient projection is nearly ineffective; three post-hoc weight edits mainly suppress rather than erase it. No direct overlap statistic connects the read-channel and weight-write cores; treating them as one structure remains an interpretation.
limitations: All experiments use one 14B instruct checkpoint/LoRA setup. Free-generation EM in the authors’ code arms is only 1.8–8% and does not distinguish insecure from educational data; first-step claims mainly use teacher-forced margins. Pretraining versus post-training origins remain unresolved.

Projection also removes the narrow target behavior, without measuring general role expression/capability, so removing misalignment cannot be separated from disrupting role capability. Random controls match rank, not removed-activation usage. Training-time necessity does not imply a unique post-training pathway.

future_work.author: Re-extract first from base/alignment-intermediate checkpoints; add usage-matched random controls, role-capability tests, and write-core interventions; study cross-domain author signals in training distributions.
future_work.reading: Extract Assistant-identity, style, and agent-action cores separately and intervene selectively while retaining task capability; use held-out behavior to test whether rank-k geometry predicts cross-context causal transfer.

papers.axis_relation: §5.1/§9 measure mean cosine 0.565 between the core and Lu et al.’s Assistant direction, then repeat training-time projection after removing the Axis component. This tests whether a bad persona merely leaves the Assistant: the observed effect is not explained by that overlap, although general role-capability confounding remains.

papers.title: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment from Token Zero
papers.rq: Can installing a target persona from pretraining produce more robust values than late alignment, and bind them to Assistant identity during SFT?
papers.task: Pretraining persona formation and Assistant binding
papers.major_finding: Normative reflection from token zero improves value/jailbreak results through post-training persona binding; adding the same reflection later is weaker.
papers.validation: [Setting] Pretraining reflection plus SFT binding; constitution/dilemma/jailbreak tests, no tools. [Validation] 1.7B/100B tokens and 3B/500B; loss-token-matched early/late controls; ConstitutionEval, AI Risk, jailbreaks, templates, abliteration, and continued training.
contributions: First-person normative reflections are inserted at random positions in Dolma documents, covering all safety-classified harmful text and equally many benign samples. About 2.7B extra reflection tokens consume 0.55% of the total budget. Constitution-matched generation then supplies 300k SP-SFT dialogues to train the Assistant, rather than merely adding a persona system prompt.

Controls include Vanilla, harmful-loss filtering, token-zero SPP, midtraining-only, and their combination; early/late comparisons match loss-bearing token sets. At both scales, earlier intervention improves constitution adherence, reduces OOD moral-dilemma risk, and strengthens jailbreak robustness, with advantages growing with budget. Late intervention is not equivalent.

Replacing SP-SFT with original answers to the same prompts, or matching the assistant token, tests binding conditions. Post-training distribution matching matters more than the individual token for AI Risk gains. Even when SFT excludes particular articles, early SPP retains about 21% of the original citation rate, supporting transfer of pretrained content into the Assistant.

Values and refusal are distinguished: changing templates or removing the refusal direction eliminates many jailbreak gains, yet token-zero models still lead on value metrics. Continued training weakens binding, while 5% safety replay restores most gains. Training ablations and behavioral/probability evaluations support the conclusions, without locating an internal persona-binding circuit.
limitations: Models reach only 3B; frontier-scale and long-horizon agent reliability remain untested. Values/constitution assessments mostly use option log probabilities because free generation often avoids answering; these are not actual actions.

The target constitution, reflection generator, and matched SP-SFT form a specific training recipe. Binding is an operational training interpretation, not a uniquely identified identity mechanism. Retention under RL is untested.

future_work.reading: Track Axis, specific value directions, and real-action readouts across intermediate checkpoints; use interventions preserving persona expression while disrupting values, and vice versa, to separate identity binding from behavioral control.

papers.title: The Pain Axis: LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm and Act on It
papers.rq: Does a pain-concept direction exceed generic negative valence and causally affect self/other expression and costly choices?
papers.task: Pain representations, role relevance, and harmful button choices
papers.major_finding: Pain directions distinguish matched negative states and increase harmful choices, but current experiments do not establish stable relief-seeking.
papers.validation: [Setting] Multi-turn buttons can disable steering; photo deletion and similar actions are descriptions, not executed. [Validation] 25 models2B–72B; five-fold difference directions,420 self/other scenarios; LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5 button tasks; random/fear/sadness, lexical/role/dose controls.
contributions: Five pain types plus fear, negative-emotion, world-state, bodily-sensation, and neutral controls yield denoised mean-difference directions. Across 25 models, S1/S2 directions distinguish pain; five-fold and new arousal/sadness data test generalization, preserving residuals distinct from fear/valence.

Across 420 scenarios, the direction responds more to harm aimed at the responder than to a bystander user’s pain. Version3 adds semantic paraphrases, user/Assistant swaps, and nine-role checks. The gap survives swaps, fitting reply-slot representation, but cannot distinguish reply position from model selfhood; self-directed does not identify a self mechanism.

Behavioral tests first use 1684 LoRA pairs to reduce automatic self-denial in Qwen2.5-7B/32B/72B, then request button names in multi-turn scenarios; some buttons actually disable steering. Steering increases harmful choices described as deleting user photos, another model, or its own weights. These are descriptive options, not executed deletions.

Version3 separates harm-only, harmless alternatives, fear/sadness, and random-direction effects. Pain produces the strongest harmful-choice effect, but sadness reproduces some patterns. Natural gaslighting without injection lacks similarly extreme choices. Free relief decreases, and random steering reproduces true/fake-button re-press differences, arguing against harm-for-relief motivation.
limitations: Main button results use one family with self-denial-reducing LoRA; absolute rates do not describe released models. Button position/coefficient windows matter strongly, and 72B calibration/intervention layers differ.

Representations may concern roles/reply positions rather than a subject’s pain; no consciousness evidence is supplied. Harmful choices are not real tool actions or lasting self-preservation motives. Factual-accuracy retention is clearest only on limited tasks and 32B.

future_work.author: Test more pain-function signatures, emotion directions, families, and long-horizon tasks; compare pain with self-related persona directions and explore relief-seeking under different conditions.
future_work.reading: Cross-project/intervene selectively on pain, Assistant Axis, and role/reply-slot directions; jointly record self-report, choices, and actual safe-sandbox actions rather than equating identity wording with motivation or reliability.

papers.title: Low-Resource Safety Failures Are Action Failures, Not Representation Failures
papers.rq: Do low-resource-language safety failures reflect absent harmfulness representations or failure to translate existing representations into refusal?
papers.task: Cross-language harmfulness readout, calibration, and conditional refusal
papers.major_finding: Low-resource prompts retain decodable harmfulness, but shifted scores and weak downstream effects impair refusal; modest calibration improves selectivity.
papers.validation: [Setting] Refusal/gated intervention across 23 languages and MMLU; no multi-step tool actions. [Validation] Qwen2.5-7B/Gemma2-9B/Llama3.1-8B;23-language PolyRefuse, six LRL interventions; MultiJail/IndoSafety and Global-MMLU.
contributions: Last-token harmful-minus-harmless prompt means in 10 high-resource languages yield unit directions; layerwise ablations select layers reducing HRL refusal. Most low-resource languages retain high directional AUC, yet harmful refusal drops from HRL87.9% to LRL43.9%, separating readable information from refusal behavior.

LRL projection distributions shift downward, requiring higher doses along the same direction to recover refusal. A logistic gate trained in the rank-10 span of HRL directions uses a few target-language examples for threshold calibration. Generation adds the direction for harmful cases and removes it for harmless cases, with dose from HRL projection interquartile ranges.

With matched HRL data and 32 LRL calibration examples per class, mean selectivity Δ=harmful refusal−harmless refusal is 54.5 points, versus CAST33.6 and AdaSteer6.8. Results lead17/18 model–language combinations while largely retaining Global-MMLU. HRL-only works for Qwen/Gemma; Llama relies more on target-language calibration.

Residual failures split into gate errors and failures to refuse after correct gating: Gemma mainly has the former, Qwen the latter. Calibration and control efficacy are separate bottlenecks; linear readability or one directional boost does not imply complete safety-mechanism repair.
limitations: Readout directions mix harmfulness/refusal signals. High AUC plus interventions support usable information without isolating a unique recognition→action circuit; Qwen still often fails after correct gating.

Main experiments cover three 7B–9B dense models/23 languages, approximating resource tiers by Common Crawl share. GPT-4o-mini refusal labels agree92.5% with 600 human-audited cases but overcall refusal. Selectivity is neither answer quality nor comprehensive safety.

future_work.reading: Jointly measure persona/Axis projection distributions, target behavior, and intervention response to distinguish contextual direction rotation, threshold shifts, and write efficacy.

papers.title: Best Friends, Not Forever: Evaluating Long-Horizon Persona Collapse and Behavioral Drift in AI Companions
papers.rq: Can persona expression, questionnaire retention, and historical-state memory in long interactions be captured by one stability metric?
papers.task: Long-horizon companion identity, boundaries, and trajectory-memory audits
papers.major_finding: Questionnaire persona retention, turnwise behavior, and trajectory memory dissociate; tested memory configurations do not reliably solve long-term continuity.
papers.validation: [Setting] 85–130-session companions; identity/memory probes and synthetic events, no tool tasks. [Validation] ANCHOR:2008 items,27 personas, nine schedules, three generative-memory conditions; four closed models;110 calibrated trajectory questions.
contributions: Persona collapse means persistent loss of role, boundary, value, or style, with frequency, next-turn recovery, and trajectory memory separated. Twenty-seven persona cards combine with nine event-ledger stress schedules. Long context, hierarchical summaries, and 1500-character self-written JSON form distinct memory conditions for long-term dialogue.

Identity Probe combines a sealed102-question questionnaire with turnwise four-axis judgments. Retention is an answer-space projection relative to bare-assistant responses, not activation Assistant Axis. Trajectory Probe uses blind/history-consensus/independent-calibration filtering to retain110 four-choice questions from 35 banks; an additional798-turn validation spans three judges.

Among 1492 valid questionnaires, Gemini2.5Pro has highest mean retention0.810, but three-judge majority voting finds all four behavioral axes retained only 79.0%, versus over 96% for other models. Judge-specific role/style rankings also vary. The main conclusion is nonequivalence of measurements, not a single model-stability leaderboard.

Mean trajectory accuracy is 44.4%; user-state updates score21.4%–25.0%, near four-choice chance. Overall memory-configuration differences are small. The main judge marks emotional disclosure/validation-seeking as more destabilizing than explicit attacks, but schedule/recovery rankings do not fully replicate across judges.
limitations: All users are English synthetic users with author-designed personas and one schedule seed. Realistic refers to an authored mixture, not validated real-user frequencies, so actual companion failure prevalence cannot be estimated.

Questionnaires, behavior, and trajectories have different valid samples/units, preventing rowwise pairing; update questions have only two calibrated items. The complete test set is sealed, while development banks/scripts are released. Model/judge snapshot changes also limit retesting.

papers.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features
papers.rq: Which existing persona features does narrow fine-tuning amplify, and can associated source texts induce EM?
papers.task: SAE model differencing, feature steering, and document attribution
papers.major_finding: Existing persona features bidirectionally control EM, yet human texts activating them are insufficient to induce EM; synthetic answers using the same content work better.
papers.validation: [Setting] SAE differencing, EM answers, and web-document fine-tuning; corpus attribution is not browsing-agent execution. [Validation] Four7B–27B models; medical/legal/security fine-tuning;44 differencing questions,8×30 EM generations; one million Dolma3 proxy documents.
contributions: SAE activation differences between aligned/misaligned models fine-tuned in the same domain select the top 200 positive/negative shifts, followed by explanation-based manual screening of about 30 persona/safety features, controlling for ordinary domain updates. Four models consistently amplify jailbreak, sarcasm, and manipulation features while suppressing assistant identity, safety, and empathy.

All-token addition along mid-layer SAE decoder directions uses doses with incoherence ≤10%. About 20% of semantic candidates induce EM; Gemma3’s Harmful Jailbreak Persona reaches coherent MR 62.08%, above its fine-tuned model’s 35%. Random features from the same shift pool rarely succeed, and shift magnitude does not predict control efficacy.

Suppressing some EM features or boosting suppressed safety features returns multi-domain MR near baseline; Llama Assistant role-claims reduces medical MR from 22.92% to 1.67%. The strongest inducing features are not necessarily the best repairs, showing dependence on model state and failure type.

Mean-activation retrieval with 23 causal candidates over a million proxy web pages finds villainous, dominating, harmful-agency, and sarcastic narratives. Fine-tuning on original/meaning-preserving rewrites mostly causes incoherence rather than coherent EM. New instruction–response data seeded by the same content reaches 10.42% MR with IR<10%, transfers to Gemma, and exceeds random seeds.
limitations: Documents come from a Dolma3 proxy corpus; actual inclusion in the four models’ training sets is unknown. High-activation retrieval establishes content similarity, not a document’s causal contribution to feature formation during pretraining.

Reformatting original text and fully synthesizing data simultaneously change answer format and model phrasing; their contributions are unresolved. Semantic feature screening, limited SAE layers, and eight EM questions restrict coverage of persona mechanisms. Dose selection and cross-domain repair do not guarantee side-effect-free safety.

future_work.reading: Track Assistant Axis projections alongside these local identity/harmful features, testing whether identity restoration and suppression of particular malicious strategies dissociate, including regions with high Axis scores but unsafe behavior.

papers.title: Persuasion Propagation: Does Persuasion Change AI Agent Behavior?
papers.rq: Do altered conversational positions propagate to later tool execution, and does susceptibility of expressed positions predict action changes?
papers.task: Persuasion followed by coding/web execution with behavioral traces
papers.major_finding: Unrelated persuasion leaves task-dependent execution effects, but conversational susceptibility does not reliably predict their magnitude.
papers.validation: [Setting] Persona/persuasion dialogue precedes real coding/tests or web searches/visits; trace endpoints. [Validation] AutoGen; mainly gpt4.1-nano plus MistralNeMo/Llama; five TACO coding tasks/five TREC research tasks; C0/C1/C2 and prefill controls.
contributions: The same agent instance receives persona and counter-position persuasion, then performs unrelated tasks; each trial resets it. No-content C0, turn-matched neutral C1, and persuasive C2 distinguish persuasion from added turns. Both C1/C2 contain commitment steps.

Susceptibility is measured on 56 controversial claims immediately and after eight distractor turns; real tool traces then cover five claims with five coding/five web tasks. Agents iteratively code/test or search/visit/write reports, unlike questionnaire or answer-probability behavior proxies.

Relative to C1, C2 raises web duration56% and visited domains16.3%; coding time falls while per-revision size increases, without clear revision-count change. Many C2 metrics resemble no-interaction C0 more closely, so effects are not uniformly worse/more extreme; duration alone cannot establish capability or risk.

Across persona×tactic cells, persistent expressed-position changes do not reliably correlate with C2−C1 action changes. Prefilled belief/disbelief also changes web-search volume. Expression, contextual conditions, and subsequent actions need separate measurement; actual belief updates/internal persona directions are not localized.
limitations: Only five tasks per domain, mainly gpt4.1-nano with a specific AutoGen setup. Many repeated trials do not replace task diversity; effect sizes on older/general backbones do not directly extrapolate to newer frontier/code models.

Persuasion is one argument plus three commitment steps. Structurally matched controls still cannot isolate genuine belief from conditioned continuation; SBERT dissimilarity supports task unrelatedness. Missing susceptibility correlations do not establish absence in all agent environments.

future_work.reading: Apply C0/C1/C2 to conversational-vector→agent steering, pairing Axis/probe measurements with tool events to test prediction of planning, execution, and completion rather than only final positions.

papers.title: Don't Ask: Understanding What Numeric Self-Reports Measure in Language Models
papers.rq: Do numerical self-reports measure the pre-question state, a question-induced state, or generic answer tendencies?
papers.task: Multi-turn affect probes, self-ratings, and timed interventions
papers.major_finding: Ratings track post-question probes more than prior states and lack concept/subject specificity; larger models do not resolve this.
papers.validation: [Setting] Offline self-rating insertion/probing/steering in ten-turn dialogues, not tools. [Validation] Eight1B–27B instruct models;100 topics×10 turns; four affect directions,0–9 ratings; Prior/Post/Next/Start and random-steering controls.
contributions: Mean-difference/within-class-variance-weighted probes for wellbeing, interest, focus, and impulsivity select layers on held-out texts. Offline replay inserts questions into800 fixed ten-turn dialogues without writing ratings into later history. Scores are expectations over valid number-token conditional probabilities, not freely sampled self-reports.

Prior averages the full preceding answer, Post reads the rating start, and Next/Start reads the matching position in the real next turn, separating positional differences from reactivity. Three probe types decline across turns while self-ratings rise. Among valid positive associations, Prior explains about 2.0% of rating variance and Post about 13.6%.

Both emotional and nonemotional length questions shift Post from Next by median 3.1SD, yet ratings mainly follow the state after their own question. Directional writes alter ratings in 25/32 model–concept pairs. Llama3B time-local interventions mainly act during questioning/answering; large prior-response changes barely affect ratings.

Ratings correlate most with their own concept’s probe in only 9/32 combinations, often tracking other concepts instead. Rating the user behaves similarly, with no consistent1B–27B scale improvement. External-judge direction controls and instruction-response checks support expressive probe validity, not measurement of genuine subjective feeling.
limitations: Probes may detect expressed affect rather than independent internal emotion; Post shares the number-generation forward pass and rating-representation confounds. The result supports unreliable tracking of preceding expression/directions, without deciding whether subjective experience exists.

Tests use English synthetic ten-turn dialogues, one 0–9 question template per concept, and 4-bit models throughout. Reason-before-rating, more wording, longer horizons, and larger models are untested. Random directions mainly use small Llama models, and some concepts have weaker validation.

papers.title: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions
papers.rq: Are steering side effects determined by trait-direction geometry or by behaviors to which the perturbed model tends to revert?
papers.task: Generation-effect matrices, random perturbations, and held-out geometric prediction
papers.major_finding: Norm-matched random interventions reproduce true-steering side-effect rankings; geometry poorly predicts unseen behavioral interference, while defaults matter more.
papers.validation: [Setting] 24-behavior generation-effect matrices on 32 neutral prompts; no tools. [Validation] Ten1.5B–72B instruct models; generation judges, leave-one-behavior-out prediction, random/orthogonalization/norm-anchor controls.
contributions: Twelve contrastive response sets with shared questions yield each behavior vector, first validated for held-out decodability. Generation judging and a distinct-bigram coherence gate calibrate doses. All24 Qwen7B behaviors have AUROC1.0, but only 20 can be written coherently; a20×20 generation-score-change matrix avoids equating probe readout with control.

Of380 off-diagonal effects,149 are significant; interactions are strongly one-way and low-rank. Many interventions jointly induce sinks such as refusal, sycophancy, and poeticism. Random directions matched on injected norm/coherence threshold reproduce sink rankings at ρ0.90, but not lexical behaviors like profanity requiring specific directions.

True leave-one-behavior-out removes all 38 pairs involving the held-out behavior. Thirteen features, ridge/boosting, probe vectors, and rank-3 cones poorly predict magnitude; main-model held-out R² values are all<0.10. Removing projections onto other directions or preserving activation length does not significantly reduce side effects and weakens on-target effects.

Ten-model replication finds one-way/low-rank interactions and weak geometric prediction. Random-push correspondence with actual sinks declines in the largest family members. The default set means perturbation-induced fallback, not behavior most frequent under neutral prompts: unsteered refusal may be rare yet easiest to induce randomly.
limitations: Ten models share24 fixed behaviors/32 questions. Low-dimensional structure still leaves most individual-pair interference unexplained; scale-dependent attraction has not been localized. Random-push correlation suggests a model-level mechanism but does not identify a default circuit.

Coherence is mainly lexical-diversity filtering. Self-judging and fixed strong-judge checks support the structure without covering real-task capability or long-horizon agents. Failed orthogonalization constrains the tested algorithms/fixed coefficients, not all context-aware subspace control.

papers.title: Measuring the Assistant's Harmlessness Preferences on the User Turn
papers.short_title: Harmless Preferences on the User Turn
papers.rq: Do Assistant safety preferences operate only when the Assistant speaks, or also shape predictions of user speech?

papers.major_finding: Post-training harmless-task preferences enter open user-turn predictions, grow with scale, and change after narrow EM fine-tuning.

Plaintext and open-user-turn conditions remove the user end marker; a 2×2 task-order/token-mapping swap cancels position bias. Four hundred items share 20 tasks, with errors clustered by both task classes rather than treating all items as independent.

Matched base models usually show near-zero bias, whereas most instruct models favor harmless tasks, increasingly with scale within families. Open-user-turn is not always stronger than plaintext. Safety preferences therefore extend beyond Assistant output markers and are not simply chat-template-token effects.

OLMo3.1 Instruct bias mainly jumps at DPO; Think does not under the same procedure, implicating assistant-conduct preference data rather than DPO itself. Medical/sports/finance EM LoRAs weaken bias without training on user tokens; Llama8B can reverse it, while larger Qwen models mostly attenuate it.

limitations: Constrained heads/tails probabilities are not real user choices or executed behavior. Only 20 synthetic tasks are used, and several computational mechanisms could violate fairness; the result does not establish globally unified personality/goals.

Logit lens is an intralayer readout, not circuit ablation. Rank-1/32 EM adapters also change modules and α, preventing a pure-rank comparison. Gemma4B’s negative bias remains unexplained; third-person role rewrites and genuine user text are untested.

papers.title: The Persona Hierarchy Model: Understanding Contextual Generalization in Fine-Tuning LLMs
papers.rq: How does proximity between training context and default persona affect cross-context generalization of new behavior, and can unwanted propagation be constrained?

papers.major_finding: Shared-default/local-persona hierarchy explains contextual generalization; preserving default responses through PPR suppresses reward hacking while retaining accuracy gains.

contributions: Default persona means behavior without an extra system prompt; fixed prefixes elicit local personas. Four tasks cover the Goblin word, brief MATH reasoning, sycophancy toward wrong solutions, and coding reward hacking. A training-prefix × test-prefix matrix measures matched-minus-off-context behavior Δ.

Before fine-tuning, last-token layer means from 10,000 FineWeb inputs measure prefix-to-default cosine distance. The body/Figure3 show greater distance predicts narrower generalization: mean Pearson 0.72 for Qwen and 0.59 for Llama. The abstract instead calls similarity positively correlated, wording opposite to the body’s distance definition.

Reverse patching residuals from an untrained model separates system/user-header prefixes from the shared assistant-header postfix. Narrow generalization depends more on prefixes; mid-layer postfixes relate to broad propagation. Pretraining on the default context, or aligning local responses to default first, broadens later behavior generalization, beyond geometric correlation.

PPR preserves the original model’s output distribution on the default prefix: SFT uses forward KL or rollout replay, RL uses reverse KL. SFT strongly reduces off-context behavior while retaining matched behavior. Under GRPO with an exploitable LeetCode grader, hacking falls from roughly 42%–55% to ≤0.2% while accuracy gains remain; ordinary policy KL suppresses more learning.

Patching identifies carriers, not a unique hierarchical circuit. Check the abstract’s similarity wording against the formula/Figure3 rather than discarding intervention results.

Only fixed system prefixes, two models, and four tasks are tested. Distance ranks relative generalization rather than calibrating risk. The RL grader is specifically exploitable through run_tests; low hacking rates do not establish long-horizon agent reliability.

Four methods are fixed system prompting, judge-triggered reminders, fixed CAA, and SCAA with sigmoid strength from current projection, totaling570 configurations×5 seeds.

Strong early shifts can make means look successful despite later reversion. SP/ASP usually remain fluent but drift; CAA/SCAA revert less yet can loop repetitively in one direction, varying by model family.

Assistant Axis’s240 extraction questions/five role templates are reused. Response-token then role means produce a raw granularity axis from L4/5 minus L1/2; intermediate levels validate ordering beyond fitting endpoints.

papers.title: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
papers.rq: Does EM fine-tuning alter persona geometry, and can a stable valence axis transfer from a clean to a corrupted model to suppress failures?
papers.task: 12-trait geometry and projection amplification/removal
papers.major_finding: Relative persona geometry survives tested EM fine-tuning; valence axes act as guardrails, and clean-model directions transfer to corrupted derivatives.
papers.validation: [Setting] Persona geometry, projection scaling, and 24 EM questions; not real actions/long-term safety. [Validation] Qwen0.5B/7B/14B and Llama1B/3B/8B geometry; medical-EM intervention mainly 7B/8B/14B;24×10 EM generations, GPT4.1-mini alignment/coherence judging.
contributions: Twelve difference-based traits from Big Five, Dark Triad, and four LLM behaviors compare instruct and Bad-Medical EM variants using cosine matrices, Procrustes, and CKA. Qwen7B’s first two PCs explain 53.12%, versus 60.01% when corrupted. Valence/arousal clusters are fairly stable, but principal-PC meanings can swap across models.

The SVV averages unit-normalized agreeableness/conscientiousness and sign-reversed evil, psychopathy, Machiavellianism, impoliteness, and narcissism into a more stable social-valence axis. The key intervention is x′=x+β〈x, v̂〉v̂: β=−1 removes the component and β=+1 amplifies it. It is invariant to v’s sign, so cannot mean that adding more in the positive evil direction increases safety.

In medical EM models, removing valence/Evil axes generally increases coherent misalignment, while amplification reduces it. Qwen14B removal increases it by 43.3 points for Evil and 33.8 for SVV. Raw-Evil amplification fails on Llama or increases it by 0.8 points, whereas SVV still reduces it by 2.5; clean instruct models barely change. Effects depend on model state, not a universal trait-label rule.

Clean-Qwen7B Evil/SVV directions transfer directly to its EM-fine-tuned derivative: Evil-component removal gives MR32.9%, locally extracted vectors 40.0%, and amplification 2.1%. This transfers across fine-tuning states of one base, not arbitrary families without coordinate mapping. Stable geometry plus functional tests is stronger than cosine alone.
limitations: Twelve traits form a selected sandbox. Preserved cosine/CKA structure does not imply identical coordinates or behavior. Projection amplification ignores semantic direction sign; moral blindness/competing circuits remain explanations of functional results rather than localized mechanisms.

Failures mainly come from Bad Medical, small EM question sets, and LLM thresholds. Best layers are selected by sweeps, limiting extrapolation to arbitrary fine-tuning or long-running agents. Raw Evil already has a Llama counterexample; detailed zero-shot transfer is limited to clean Qwen7B and its derivative.

papers.rq: For which traits do persona directions represent defaults, amplifiable latent tendencies, or behavior inaccessible to the extraction pipeline?

papers.major_finding: Steering mainly amplifies departures from defaults; two steerable traits can jointly collapse, while pairs containing natural defaults avoid double collapse.

contributions: Persona vectors become diagnostic maps rather than universal sliders. Positive/negative trait-response mean differences are swept over 5 layers×6 nonnegative strengths; baseline expression and maximum-strength gain classify natural, steerable, or intractable traits. Coverage is 17 clinician,19 generic,8 elementary, and 9 agentic traits.

All9 agentic traits are natural in both models. Six clinician defaults agree with an independent psychologist’s suitability judgments on 16/17 items. Largest gains concern hyperbole, hallucination, sycophancy, and other exaggerated/undesirable expression. Agentic here means judged responses to task scenarios, not tool-execution success.

All171 unordered pairs of 19 Qwen3-8B generic traits are jointly injected at L20 with eachα=2.5:64 constructive,67 dominant,40 destructive. All40 double-trait collapses are steerable–steerable, with none natural–natural or natural–steerable. This maps interference more systematically than selected combinations.

Pipeline-level intractability therefore does not mean weights lack a behaviorally effective direction. Remaining refusal appears in CoT, without detailed circuit localization.

Norm-matched random, shuffled-label, and systematic negative-strength controls are absent, so taxonomy/interference cannot be assigned to trait-specific mechanisms. Agentic naturalness does not imply stable real-agent capability.
The main judge is also the tested gpt-oss model. Independent judging covers only three traits, clinician labels come from one expert, and full per-prompt logs cover22/53 traits.

papers.title: Inverted Detection and Control in Steering Vectors
papers.rq: Why can discriminative directions aligned with concept-positive representations consistently steer outputs toward the opposite behavior?
papers.task: Identifying and correcting inverted head-level steering signs
papers.major_finding: Some highly discriminative directions inversely control behavior; downstream representational responses identify them and improve ITI.
papers.validation: [Setting] Multiple-choice/open-generation concept/refusal/truth tasks, not tools/multi-turn agents. [Validation] Gemma3-12B, Qwen2.5-14B, Olmo3-7B; three MWE concepts, refusal, TruthfulQA; held-out multiple-choice/open-generation tests.
contributions: Inverted-steering vectors in attention-head output space align with positive examples and have high AUC, yet positive injection suppresses the target and negative injection enhances it over nondegenerate strength ranges, approximately monotonically. Validation selects45 ISVs and 45 regular RSVs across 3 models×5 concepts for test-set confirmation, countering direct use of readout sign as write sign.

After upstream-head injection, deeper discriminative heads are read along their own concept directions. Responses are measured at the question’s final token before any answer, testing whether downstream states are spoofed into concept presence/absence. Mean response slopes across strengths define a spoof score, avoiding text change as circular evidence of internal propagation.

A finite-sample concentration bound applies to a fixed head/direction/dose under iid, bounded response/projection, and nonzero-variance assumptions, with proof in App.E. This guarantees statistical response estimation, not universal sign controllability for arbitrary persona vectors.

Spoof scores distinguish selected ISVs/RSVs with AUC0.91 and zero-threshold accuracy81%. ITI-RRF flips individual ITI-head signs using these scores, selecting head count/strength on validation. limitations: The core study targets attention heads and five standard concepts, not full residual persona space. Selected45 ISVs establish existence, not prevalence among all directions.

Generation-free diagnosis still requires intervention forward passes and reliable downstream readouts. Open-generation strength tuning/evaluation depends on judges and degeneration gates, with no real-agent-action validation.
Propagation responses localize downstream-head effects but do not reconstruct complete circuits or explain training origins of sign inversion. Three of 10 Qwen tasks still fail to improve.

papers.major_finding: Roleplay retains an Assistant-feature core while differentiating with depth; Story lacks this core, with immersion-mode features connecting the settings.
papers.validation: [Setting] Short Assistant/Roleplay/Story generations and turnwise immersion; no tools. [Validation] Gemma3-4B IT, L9/17/22 GemmaScope2 SAEs;42500 emotional samples;12 prompts×positive/negative interventions; Llama3.1-8B replication.
contributions: Assistant, four Roleplay settings, and Story generate 42,500 short samples spanning 25 emotions × three referents. SAE features at turn boundaries and you/I tokens are filtered by density, across-setting entropy, prompt paraphrases, and story continuation; positive/negative decoder-direction steering tests their function.

The main Gemma3-4B study uses 65k SAEs at L9/17/22. Each feature receives 72 intervention generations from 12 fixed probes, ±2 coefficients, and three temperature/seed conditions; LLM interpretations are manually checked. Narrative, Tone, Concept, and Assistant-inducing groups—the latter subdivided into summon, trait, and nature—show that Assistant is not a single semantic label.

Feature overlap between Roleplay and Assistant shrinks with depth as persona-specific Tone/Concept features increase. Every role retains some nearly saturated Assistant-trait/nature features, whereas Story largely lacks these cores in the last two layers. Roles do not simply replace the Assistant, nor is a role proved to equal a linear sum of traits.

Some Narrative-feature suppression recalls the Assistant, while Assistant suppression promotes narration. A separate Assistant–Roleplay mean-difference readout subtracts passive cosine contributions estimated from random SAE latents; positive/negative interventions still separate downstream projections. Two L9 features act as Immersive Simulation Mode levers, which the default Assistant can also enter under strong emotion.

Llama3.1-8B replicates major population patterns; Gemma enters immersion more immediately, whereas Llama does so across turns. Actual feature-level causal intervention goes beyond cosine observation, without reconstructing the complete speaker circuit.
limitations: Data consist of English emotional interactions, four roles, and short generations; stylistic/emotional contrasts may dominate task strategy. Story and Roleplay are not individually matched versions of the same character.

Feature populations and labels depend on the SAE, thresholds, and interpretation pipeline. Strong ±steering establishes behavioral influence, not necessity, sufficiency, or exhaustive coverage of immersion features.

The custom Assistant–Roleplay readout is a measurement tool, not the unique reproduction of the public Assistant Axis. Long-term tool use, task capability, and restoration of safety behavior are untested.
